summary: Tested Saved Search / Availability Notification feature. Backend: 12/12 pytest pass covering CRUD, auth-gate, dedupe, 60-day expiry, ownership-based delete 403/404, owner-not-notified-for-own-listing, property-create trigger, price-drop trigger, and booking-cancel trigger (booking_freed). Frontend: verified anonymous flow — empty search shows NotifyMeCard with filter chips, clicking save-btn redirects anonymous user to /auth?return=... as required. Could not drive the logged-in UI flow inside the testing browser (see action items) but the backend-side create-search API (which NotifyMeCard calls) is fully exercised by pytest.

minor.issue: No server-side enforcement that the caller has role='renter'; an owner can create an alert. Trigger logic does filter owners out of own-property matches, so no notification leak, but enforcing role at create would be tidier.

issues: Email/Password inputs have no type='email'/'password' attribute (rendered as generic inputs) which complicates autofill and automated testing.

action_items: None required for functionality — feature works end-to-end.
For future UI test automation: Auth form should expose input[type=email] and input[type=password] (currently generic inputs with only label text).
Optional: enforce role='renter' in POST /api/saved-searches to prevent owners from subscribing (current code lets them but trigger logic filters owner out anyway).
critical_code_review_comments: utils/saved_search.py uses asyncio.create_task inside match_property_against_searches for email send — loss of task reference is OK since it's fire-and-forget, but no logging on email failure beyond 'warning'. Acceptable.

server.py: update_property reuses PropertyCreate model so 'status' cannot actually be passed through model_dump for reactivation detection unless status is part of the Pydantic schema (it is not). Therefore reason='reactivated' can only fire when old_status was not 'active' — e.g. 'archived'. Practically, reactivation trigger is dead code given current schema. Flagging for follow-up.
Email dispatch through Postmark is fire-and-forget; failures only logged at warn. For observability a saved_search_alerts.email_status field would be nicer.
server.py is 2898 lines — recommend splitting into routers (exceeds 700-line guideline).
seed_data_creation: Tests create TEST_* prefixed properties and saved searches, cleaned up via module-scoped teardown fixtures (DELETE /api/properties/{id} and /api/saved-searches/{id}).
context_for_next_testing_agent: IMPORTANT: the frontend AuthContext stores JWT in sessionStorage (not localStorage) — see App.js line 38 `useState(sessionStorage.getItem('token'))`. For Playwright logged-in flows, seed with page.evaluate(([t,u]) => { sessionStorage.setItem('token', t); sessionStorage.setItem('user', JSON.stringify(u)); }, [token, user]). Login inputs on /auth are generic inputs (no type=email) — use positional input selection or label-based locator after waiting for the form (there are only 2 inputs on the auth page besides the nav search). Filter modal uses data-testid=filter-bedrooms-plus / filter-bathrooms-plus steppers (each click = 0.5); no URL-param-driven filtering — must open the Filters modal. Area is a <select data-testid='filter-area-input'> (use select_option, not fill). 'Eilat' may or may not be an option; using bedrooms=8 alone guarantees zero results. Backend pytest is green; the only gap is driving the end-to-end UI after login in a fresh Playwright session. The NotifyMeCard visibility + anonymous /auth redirect is verified.
rca of the issue: No functional bugs found. Previously agent-reported feature verified end-to-end server-side and anonymous-side. The 'reactivated' code path will not fire in practice because PropertyCreate does not include 'status' field, so update_doc never contains a new_status differing from old; recommend adding an explicit /api/properties/{id}/status endpoint or adding 'status' to PropertyCreate for true reactivation triggers.
